messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Turkish, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Turkish line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.
Yüksekte baktım ve omuzlarını gördüm Zaten gezegenin ışınlarıyla kaplı Ki, her yolda insanları doğru yönlendirir.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑by‑Word Mapping Table**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Word / Phrase | Back‑Translation (EN) | Status | |-------------|-----------------------|----------------------|------------------------|--------| | guardai | “I looked” (perfect) | **baktım** | I looked | OK | | in | preposition “in” (direction) | **Yüksekte** (locative suffix) | (in) high | UNNECESSARY | | alto | “high” (location) | **Yüksekte** | high (loc.) | OK | | e | coordinating “and” | **ve** | and | OK | | vidi | “I saw” (perfect) | **gördüm** | I saw | OK | | le | definite article (fem. pl.) | – (omitted) | the | UNNECESSARY | | sue | possessive “its” (referring to shoulders) | **omuzlarını** (possessive‑accusative) | its shoulders | OK | | spalle | “shoulders” (acc.) | **omuzlarını** | shoulders | OK | | vestite | “clothed / covered” (participle) | **kaplı** | clothed | OK | | già | adverb “already” | **Zaten** | already | OK | | de' | preposition “of” (genitive) | – (genitive suffix on *gezegenin*) | of | UNNECESSARY | | raggi | “rays” (source of light) | **ışınlarıyla** (with rays) | rays (with) | OK | | del | preposition “of the” (genitive) | – (genitive suffix on *gezegenin*) | of the | UNNECESSARY | | pianeta | “planet” (genitive) | **gezegenin** | of the planet | OK | | che | relative pronoun “that/which” | **Ki** | that | OK | | mena | “leads / guides” (present) | **yönlendirir** | leads | OK | | dritto | adverb “straight / aright” | **doğru** | straight | OK | | altrui | “people / men” (indirect object) | **insanları** | people | OK | | per | preposition “along / for” | – (expressed by case in *yolda*) | along | UNNECESSARY | | ogne | adjective “every” | **her** | every | OK | | calle | “path / road” (acc.) | **yolda** (locative) | path | OK |

### Items Requiring Attention - **UNNECESSARY**: `in`, `le`, `de'`, `del`, `per` – Turkish encodes these relations via case endings or omits articles, so separate lexical items are not needed. - **MISSING / WRONG / GRAMMAR**: none detected.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only Turkish script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Turkish text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).
